text: Scaled Agile Framework came out of the desire to figure out how do we scale Scrum and different processes. I do not recommend using SAFe.
speaker: Melissa Perri
context: Lenny asks Melissa about SAFe (Scaled Agile Framework), which is a methodology for implementing agile practices at large organizations. SAFe is a structured approach that provides detailed frameworks and processes for coordinating multiple development teams. Melissa explains her strong opposition to using SAFe as prescribed, noting that even organizations that claim success with it ultimately modify it so extensively that it no longer resembles the original framework.
text_ko: 스케일드 애자일 프레임워크(Scaled Agile Framework, SAFe)는 우리가 스크럼(Scrum)과 여러 프로세스를 어떻게 확장할지 알아내고자 하는 욕구에서 나온 거예요. 다만 저는 SAFe 사용을 권하지 않아요. 제가 만나서 얘기해본 사람들 중 SAFe를 좋아하거나 SAFe로 성공했다고 말한 분들은 전부 결국 그 프레임워크를 다 뜯어고쳐서 자기들만의 방식으로 바꿔버리더라고요.
text_zh: 规模化敏捷框架(Scaled Agile Framework)当初就是想解决一个问题：怎么把Scrum这些流程放大到更大规模。但我真的不建议用SAFe。我接触过的每一个说SAFe好用、用SAFe成功了的人，到最后都把它拆得七零八落，改成了别的东西。
text_es: El Scaled Agile Framework (SAFe) surgió de la necesidad de descifrar cómo escalar Scrum y otros procesos. Pero te digo que no recomiendo usar SAFe. Cada persona con la que he hablado que le gustó SAFe, que tuvo éxito con SAFe, al final terminó deshaciéndose de todo eso y convirtiéndolo en algo completamente diferente.
key_sentence: I do not recommend using SAFe.
original_text: Scaled Agile Framework came out of the desire to figure out how do we scale Scrum and different processes. I do not recommend using SAFe. Every single person I have talked to who likes SAFe, found success with SAFe, they ended up ripping it up and making it into something else.

vocabulary.definition: To increase or decrease in size, amount, or capacity, often in a systematic manner.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and technology, scaling refers to the ability of a company or system to grow and manage increased demand without compromising performance.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'scale' often implies growth, it can also refer to the ability to efficiently handle larger operations without losing quality.

vocabulary.definition: A structured approach or system that provides guidance and support for achieving specific goals or outcomes.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, frameworks are often used to standardize processes, enhance collaboration, and ensure that all team members are aligned with organizational objectives.
vocabulary.nuance: The term 'framework' suggests a flexible structure that can be adapted to various situations, rather than a rigid set of rules.

vocabulary.definition: A systematic, theoretical analysis of the methods applied to a field of study or practice.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and project management, a methodology outlines the processes and techniques used to achieve project objectives, ensuring consistency and efficiency.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'methodology' implies a formalized approach, it can also encompass a range of practices that may not be strictly defined.

vocabulary.definition: The act of putting a plan or decision into effect; executing a strategy or process.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, implementing refers to the execution of strategies, policies, or technologies to achieve desired outcomes and improve operations.
vocabulary.nuance: The term 'implementing' often carries a connotation of careful planning and execution, distinguishing it from mere execution without consideration.

text: A lot of large companies turn to Scrum or to the frameworks, and it's because they traditionally didn't grow up building software.
speaker: Melissa Perri
context: Lenny asks why some companies need these frameworks while others (like Silicon Valley startups) seem to build great products without them. Melissa explains that large, traditional companies (banks, telecoms, etc.) turn to structured frameworks because they lack experience building software natively. She emphasizes that the core agile principles of speed and customer value are sound, but rigid adherence to processes can be counterproductive.
text_ko: 많은 대기업이 스크럼(Scrum)이나 여러 프레임워크들(frameworks)에 의지하는 건, 전통적으로 소프트웨어를 직접 만들어온 조직이 아니었기 때문이에요. 애자일 방법론(agile methodologies)을 보면 핵심은 빠르게 움직여 고객에게 큰 가치를 제공하자는 거예요. 그 원칙들을 받아들이면 잘 해낼 거예요.
text_zh: 很多大公司都开始用Scrum或者各种框架(framework)，主要是因为他们以前不是做软件出身的。你看敏捷开发方法(agile methodologies)，说白了就是我们希望能快速行动，给客户带来真正的价值。如果你能抓住这些核心理念，肯定能做得不错。
text_es: Muchas empresas grandes recurren a Scrum o a estos frameworks, y es porque tradicionalmente no crecieron desarrollando software. Cuando ves las metodologías ágiles, lo que realmente estamos diciendo ahí es que queremos poder movernos rápido y entregar gran valor a los clientes. Si abrazas esos principios, te va a ir bien.
key_sentence: Companies turn to Scrum because they didn't grow up building software.
original_text: A lot of large companies turn to Scrum or to the frameworks, and it's because they traditionally didn't grow up building software. When you look at agile methodologies, what we're really saying there is we want to be able to move quickly and deliver great value to customers. If you embrace those principles, you're going to do well.

vocabulary.definition: Frameworks are structured systems or guidelines that provide a foundation for developing software applications or managing projects. They help streamline processes and ensure consistency across different teams and projects.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and technology, frameworks like Scrum or Agile provide methodologies for project management, enabling teams to collaborate effectively and adapt to changing requirements.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'frameworks' can refer to any structured approach, in tech, it often implies a formalized method that enhances efficiency and productivity.

vocabulary.definition: Traditionally refers to practices or methods that have been established and followed over a long period, often based on historical precedent. It implies a sense of continuity and adherence to established norms.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, 'traditionally' is used to describe long-standing practices that may contrast with modern or innovative approaches, highlighting the evolution of industry standards.
vocabulary.nuance: The term can carry a connotation of resistance to change, suggesting that something may be outdated or less effective in contemporary settings.

vocabulary.definition: Building refers to the process of creating or developing something, particularly in the context of constructing physical structures or developing software applications. It encompasses planning, execution, and refinement.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the tech industry, 'building' often describes the development of software products, emphasizing the iterative nature of creating functional and user-friendly applications.
vocabulary.nuance: The term suggests a hands-on, constructive approach, and is often used in contrast to merely conceptualizing or discussing ideas without implementation.

vocabulary.definition: Products are tangible or intangible items offered to consumers or businesses, designed to meet specific needs or demands in the market. They can range from physical goods to software applications and services.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business setting, 'products' refer to the outputs of a company that are marketed to customers, and their development is central to business strategy and revenue generation.
vocabulary.nuance: The term can imply a focus on marketability and consumer needs, and is often used in discussions about innovation, competition, and value proposition.

text: This product owner role did not emerge from product management as we know it today. It was a way to help the developers prioritize what to work on.
speaker: Melissa Perri
context: Lenny mentions his surprise at seeing product owner as one of the fastest-growing roles in tech, despite never encountering it in his circles. Melissa explains the origins of the product owner role, clarifying that it emerged from Scrum methodology to help developers with prioritization, not from traditional product management practices. She discovered this disconnect when speaking at agile conferences where she learned about this parallel evolution of product roles.
text_ko: 이 프로덕트 오너 역할(product owner role)은 지금 우리가 아는 프로덕트 매니지먼트(product management)에서 바로 나온 건 아니었어요. 원래는 개발자들이 무엇을 먼저 작업할지 우선순위를 정하도록 돕기 위한 방식이었죠. 결국 저는 수많은 애자일 컨퍼런스(agile conferences)에 가서 프로덕트 매니지먼트(product management)에 대해 발표를 했고, 그 과정에서 스크럼(Scrum) 안에 이런 프로덕트 오너 역할(product owner role)이 있다는 걸 알게 됐어요.
text_zh: 这个产品负责人(product owner)的角色其实不是从我们现在理解的产品管理里发展出来的。当时就是为了帮开发人员搞清楚优先级，知道先做什么后做什么。后来我跑了好多敏捷开发(agile)的会议，去讲产品管理的事儿，慢慢才发现原来Scrum里面有这么个产品负责人的角色。
text_es: Este rol de product owner no surgió del product management como lo conocemos hoy. Era una forma de ayudar a los desarrolladores a priorizar en qué trabajar. Terminé yendo a un montón de conferencias ágiles hablando sobre gestión de productos, y ahí fue cuando empecé a enterarme de que existía este rol de product owner en Scrum.
key_sentence: It was a way to help the developers prioritize what to work on.
original_text: This product owner role did not emerge from product management as we know it today. It was a way to help the developers prioritize what to work on. I ended up going to a ton of agile conferences and speaking about product management, and I started to learn that there was this product owner role in Scrum.

vocabulary.definition: To arrange or deal with tasks or items in order of importance or urgency.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and project management, prioritizing is essential for effective resource allocation and ensuring that critical tasks are completed first to meet deadlines and objectives.
vocabulary.nuance: While prioritizing implies a systematic approach to decision-making, it can sometimes suggest that less important tasks may be overlooked or delayed.

vocabulary.definition: To come into view or become apparent after being concealed or not previously known.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the context of business and innovation, new trends, technologies, or roles often emerge in response to changing market demands or organizational needs.
vocabulary.nuance: Emerge often conveys a sense of gradual development or revelation, suggesting that the subject was not previously recognized or understood.

vocabulary.definition: The function or position that an individual or entity holds within a particular context or organization.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business setting, clearly defined roles are crucial for delineating responsibilities, enhancing collaboration, and ensuring accountability among team members.
vocabulary.nuance: The term role can imply a level of expectation and responsibility, and it may vary significantly across different organizations or projects.

vocabulary.definition: The organizational function responsible for guiding the development, marketing, and lifecycle of a product from conception to market delivery.
vocabulary.businessContext: In tech and startup environments, product management plays a critical role in aligning product strategy with customer needs and business goals, often acting as a bridge between engineering, design, and marketing teams.
vocabulary.nuance: Product management encompasses both strategic and tactical elements, and its effectiveness can significantly influence a product's success in the market.

text: What I found was that there was a really big misconception about what those people should be doing compared to what they teach in agile and Scrum versus what we all consider great product management.
speaker: Melissa Perri
context: Melissa describes her experience training product owners at large companies during agile transformations around 2014-2015. She discovered that people from various backgrounds (developers, business analysts, project managers) were suddenly designated as product owners without proper training in actual product management principles. This created a significant gap between what these newly-minted product owners were doing versus what constitutes effective product management.
text_ko: 제가 발견한 건, 애자일(agile)과 스크럼(Scrum)에서 가르치는 것과 우리가 생각하는 훌륭한 제품 관리 사이에, 그 역할을 맡은 분들이 실제로 해야 할 일에 대해 큰 오해가 있다는 점이에요. 지난 거의 10년 동안 여기서 여러 회사들과 일하면서 그 간극을 메우려고 노력해왔어요.
text_zh: 我发现有个很大的误区，就是关于这些人应该做什么，敏捷(agile)和Scrum里教的那套，跟我们认为的优秀产品管理(product management)之间，差距挺大的。过去快10年，我一直在跟这些公司合作，想要填补这个空白。
text_es: Lo que me di cuenta es que había una confusión bastante grande sobre lo que esa gente debería estar haciendo comparado con lo que enseñan en agile y Scrum versus lo que todos consideramos una buena gestión de producto. He estado tratando de cerrar esa brecha durante casi 10 años trabajando con estas empresas aquí.
key_sentence: There's a really big misconception about agile practices versus great product management.
original_text: What I found was that there was a really big misconception about what those people should be doing compared to what they teach in agile and Scrum versus what we all consider great product management. I've been trying to fill that gap for the last almost 10 years working with these companies here.

vocabulary.definition: A misunderstanding or incorrect belief about a particular subject or situation.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business settings, misconceptions can lead to poor decision-making and ineffective strategies, particularly when stakeholders have differing views on processes or roles.
vocabulary.nuance: While often used to describe a general misunderstanding, it can imply a need for clarification or education to rectify the belief.

vocabulary.definition: A methodology that promotes iterative development, flexibility, and collaboration in project management, particularly in software development.
vocabulary.businessContext: In tech and startup environments, agile practices enable teams to respond quickly to changes and deliver value incrementally, enhancing productivity and customer satisfaction.
vocabulary.nuance: The term can also imply a cultural shift towards adaptability and continuous improvement, beyond just the framework itself.

vocabulary.definition: The process of guiding the development, marketing, and lifecycle of a product to meet customer needs and business objectives.
vocabulary.businessContext: In startups and tech companies, effective product management is crucial for aligning cross-functional teams and ensuring that products deliver value to users while achieving strategic goals.
vocabulary.nuance: It encompasses a blend of strategic thinking, market analysis, and user experience design, often requiring a balance between technical and business skills.

vocabulary.definition: A significant change or overhaul in structure, strategy, or operations, often aimed at improving efficiency or adapting to new market conditions.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, transformation initiatives can involve digital transformation, cultural shifts, or process reengineering to enhance competitiveness and innovation.
vocabulary.nuance: The term often implies a comprehensive and strategic approach, rather than incremental changes, and can evoke both excitement and resistance among stakeholders.

text: When I've worked with companies on digital transformations, you want a development operating model. That's where a lot of these agile methodologies came out of.
speaker: Melissa Perri
context: Lenny asks for advice on how leaders should approach digital transformation instead of adopting SAFe. Melissa explains that agile methodologies only address the development operating model - how teams build software - but don't solve the broader challenges of product strategy, go-to-market execution, and comprehensive product management. She emphasizes that organizations need to think beyond just development processes.
text_ko: 디지털 전환을 진행하는 기업들과 일해보면 개발 운영 모델(development operating model)이 필요하다고 느끼게 돼요. 많은 애자일 방법론(agile methodologies)도 바로 거기서 나온 거고요. 다만 그건 어디까지나 개발 운영 모델일 뿐이라 시장 진입(go-to-market), 제품 출시나 제품 관리(product management)에는 직접적인 도움이 되지는 않아요.
text_zh: 我跟一些公司合作做数字化转型的时候，你得有一个开发运营模式。很多敏捷方法论(agile methodologies)就是从这儿来的。但你要明白，这只是开发运营模式，对你的市场推广(go-to-market)、产品发布，还有产品管理其实帮不上什么忙。
text_es: Cuando he trabajado con empresas en transformaciones digitales, necesitas un modelo operativo de desarrollo. De ahí es donde salieron muchas de estas metodologías ágiles. Tienes que entender que eso es solo el modelo operativo de desarrollo, eso en realidad no te va a ayudar con el go-to-market, con lanzar tus productos ni con la gestión de productos.
key_sentence: Agile methodologies came out of the development operating model, not go-to-market strategies.
original_text: When I've worked with companies on digital transformations, you want a development operating model. That's where a lot of these agile methodologies came out of. You have to understand that's just the development operating model, that's not actually going to help you with go-to-market, with launching your products and with product management.

vocabulary.definition: The process of integrating digital technology into all areas of a business, fundamentally changing how it operates and delivers value to customers.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business settings, digital transformation often involves adopting new technologies to improve efficiency, enhance customer experiences, and create new business models.
vocabulary.nuance: While often associated with technology upgrades, it also encompasses cultural shifts within organizations to embrace change and innovation.

vocabulary.definition: A framework that outlines how an organization delivers value, including its structure, processes, and governance.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the context of business, an operating model is crucial for aligning resources and capabilities with strategic objectives, particularly during transformations.
vocabulary.nuance: The term can imply a level of rigidity, so it's important to adapt the operating model to changing business environments.

vocabulary.definition: A set of principles and practices for software development that emphasize flexibility, collaboration, and customer feedback.
vocabulary.businessContext: In tech and startup environments, agile methodologies are used to enhance project management and product development, allowing teams to respond quickly to changes and customer needs.
vocabulary.nuance: While agile methodologies promote speed and adaptability, they require a cultural commitment to collaboration and iterative processes.

vocabulary.definition: The process of creating, improving, or expanding products, services, or capabilities within an organization.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, development can refer to software development, product development, or organizational development, all aimed at enhancing competitiveness and market relevance.
vocabulary.nuance: The term can be broad, so specifying the type of development (e.g., product, software) is often necessary for clarity.

text: I'd say there's a lot of things you can do to help move your companies forward, and I have seen in a lot of these organizations too, a groundswell of product owners and product managers saying, 'Hey, what's next for me?
speaker: Melissa Perri
context: Lenny asks what advice Melissa has for product owners who want to advance their careers and become more strategic. Melissa encourages people to speak up about career development and push for more strategic responsibilities. She explains that when multiple employees raise these concerns, it creates organizational pressure that forces leadership to address career pathing and role clarity issues.
text_ko: 제가 보기엔 회사를 앞으로 나아가게 하려면 할 수 있는 일이 정말 많아요. 그리고 많은 조직에서 프로덕트 오너(product owners)랑 프로덕트 매니저(product managers)들이 '다음엔 내가 뭘 하지? 지금 무슨 일이 벌어지고 있는 거지?'라고 묻기 시작하는 큰 흐름이 생기는 것도 많이 봤어요. 그런 분위기가 조직을 움직여서 스스로 답을 찾아내게 만들어요.
text_zh: 我觉得有很多事情可以帮助推动公司向前发展，而且我在很多组织里都看到，产品负责人(product owners)和产品经理(product managers)开始主动问："嘿，我下一步该怎么走？接下来会发生什么？"正是这种声音让组织开始思考并找出解决方案。
text_es: Yo diría que hay muchas cosas que puedes hacer para impulsar a tus empresas hacia adelante, y también he visto en muchas de estas organizaciones un movimiento desde abajo donde los product owners y product managers están diciendo: "Oye, ¿qué sigue para mí? ¿Qué está pasando?" Y eso hace que las organizaciones se pongan las pilas y lo resuelvan.
key_sentence: A groundswell of product owners helps move your companies forward and figure it out.
original_text: I'd say there's a lot of things you can do to help move your companies forward, and I have seen in a lot of these organizations too, a groundswell of product owners and product managers saying, 'Hey, what's next for me? What's going on?' That makes the organizations go and figure it out.

vocabulary.definition: A significant increase in public support or interest, often emerging organically from a grassroots level.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, a groundswell can indicate a rising demand for certain products or services, often driven by consumer feedback or market trends.
vocabulary.nuance: The term often carries a positive connotation, suggesting a movement that is both powerful and authentic, making it suitable for discussions about innovation or change.

vocabulary.definition: Relating to the identification of long-term or overall aims and interests and the means of achieving them.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the corporate world, strategic planning is essential for aligning resources and actions with the organization's goals and market opportunities.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'strategic' implies careful planning and foresight, it can sometimes be viewed as overly calculated or rigid if not balanced with flexibility.

vocabulary.definition: To move forward in position, progress, or development; to promote or facilitate growth.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, advancing can refer to the progression of projects, initiatives, or individual careers within an organization.
vocabulary.nuance: The term often implies a proactive approach and can be used in both positive and neutral contexts, depending on the situation.

vocabulary.definition: To express one's opinion or concerns openly and assertively, especially in a group setting.
vocabulary.businessContext: Encouraging employees to speak up is vital for fostering a culture of transparency and innovation within organizations, allowing for diverse perspectives.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'speak up' is generally seen as a positive action, it may be perceived as confrontational in certain hierarchical or conservative environments.

text: When I think of product operating models and what I do with companies is we break out how do you determine product strategy? Do you have a good product strategy? You look at your organizational design. How are we actually organized around our products?
speaker: Melissa Perri
context: Continuing her advice on digital transformation, Melissa outlines her framework for building effective product operating models. Instead of just focusing on development processes like SAFe does, she emphasizes the need to examine product strategy, organizational structure, and ensuring proper coverage of skilled product managers throughout the organization. This represents a more holistic approach to transformation than just implementing agile frameworks.
text_ko: 제가 프로덕트 운영 모델(product operating models)을 생각하고 회사들과 일할 때는, 제품 전략(product strategy)을 어떻게 정하는지부터 세부적으로 나눠서 봐요. 좋은 제품 전략이 있는지, 조직 설계(organizational design)는 어떤지 살펴보고요. 실제로 제품을 중심으로 어떻게 조직되어 있는지, 프로덕트 매니저(product managers)가 충분히 배치돼 있는지, 조직 전반에 걸쳐 능력 있는 프로덕트 매니저들이 있는지도 확인해요.
text_zh: 说到产品运营模式(product operating models)，我跟公司合作的时候会拆解几个问题：你们怎么制定产品策略的？产品策略做得好不好？还要看组织架构设计，就是围绕产品我们的组织架构搭得怎么样？产品经理的覆盖面够不够，从上到下各个层级的产品经理水平行不行？
text_es: Cuando pienso en modelos operativos de producto y lo que hago con las empresas es que desglosamos: ¿cómo determinas tu estrategia de producto? ¿Tienes una buena estrategia de producto? Miras el diseño organizacional. ¿Cómo estamos realmente organizados alrededor de nuestros productos? ¿Tenemos buena cobertura de product managers y tenemos product managers capacitados en toda la organización?
key_sentence: We break out how to determine product strategy and ensure good coverage of product managers.
original_text: When I think of product operating models and what I do with companies is we break out how do you determine product strategy? Do you have a good product strategy? You look at your organizational design. How are we actually organized around our products? Do we have good coverage of product managers and do we have skilled product managers up and down the organization?

vocabulary.definition: Operating models refer to the framework that outlines how an organization delivers value through its processes, people, and technology.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and tech environments, operating models are crucial for aligning resources and capabilities with strategic objectives, ensuring efficiency and effectiveness in operations.
vocabulary.nuance: The term often implies a structured approach to operations, and is typically used in discussions about improving efficiency or implementing change.

vocabulary.definition: Organizational design is the process of structuring an organization in a way that aligns its resources and capabilities with its strategic goals.
vocabulary.businessContext: In startups and established companies alike, effective organizational design is essential for fostering collaboration, enhancing communication, and achieving operational efficiency.
vocabulary.nuance: This term often carries a connotation of intentionality and strategic planning, and is frequently discussed in the context of change management.

vocabulary.definition: Product strategy is a plan that outlines the vision, goals, and tactics for developing and marketing a product to meet customer needs and achieve business objectives.
vocabulary.businessContext: In tech and startup settings, a well-defined product strategy is critical for guiding product development, prioritizing features, and aligning teams around a common goal.
vocabulary.nuance: The term suggests a long-term perspective and is often used in discussions about market positioning and competitive advantage.

vocabulary.definition: Digital transformation refers to the integration of digital technology into all areas of a business, fundamentally changing how it operates and delivers value to customers.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the context of business and technology, digital transformation is often pursued to enhance efficiency, improve customer experiences, and stay competitive in a rapidly evolving market.
vocabulary.nuance: This term implies a significant shift in operations and culture, and is typically associated with innovation and modernization efforts.
